n: The Lord calls the elders in Kirtland to listen closely. Some members had been swayed by a woman named Hubble who claimed to receive revelations for the Church, and this revelation answers that confusion.
The Lord reminds the elders that they already received “a law” for the Church (D&C 42) through the one he appointed—Joseph Smith. Revelation for the whole Church comes through a recognized channel.

f.w: a commandment for a law unto my church

n: While Joseph remains faithful, no one else is appointed to receive commandments for the Church. The phrase “if he abide in me” makes clear the calling depends on his faithfulness.
Even if Joseph lost this gift, he would still be the one to appoint his successor. The Lord’s house has an orderly line of authority; it cannot be seized by self-proclaimed prophets.

f.g: In his stead = in his place.

n: As a standing rule, the Saints are not to accept anyone who arrives claiming to bring revelations or commandments for the Church outside this channel.
This rule protects the Saints from deception and gives them a clear test for recognizing teachings that are not from God.

f.w: that you may not be deceived

n: Those truly called “come in at the gate”—they are properly ordained, as the Lord explained before—and teach the revelations given through the appointed prophet. Compare Jesus’s image of the true shepherd entering by the door.
When the elders meet, they are to teach and strengthen one another so they know how to lead the Church and live its laws. Meetings are for mutual learning, not just listening.
Learning the Lord’s law is meant to make them holy. They are to commit themselves to act “in all holiness.”

f.g: Made holy, purified and set apart for God.

n: Faithfulness brings added glory; neglect means losing even what they have. This echoes the Savior’s principle that those who use what they receive are given more.

f.w: it shall be taken, even that which ye have received

n: The elders must root out sin among them and prepare themselves spiritually before God.
To receive the kingdom’s glories, the Saints are to sustain Joseph Smith and support him through faith-filled prayer. Sustaining a prophet is an active commitment.

f.w: uphold him before me by the prayer of faith

n: If they want deeper revelation, they should provide Joseph with food, clothing, and what he needs for his work. At this time Joseph had no regular income and was laboring on the Bible translation.
If they fail to support him, he will stay with those who do receive him. The Lord is gathering a “pure people,” and the blessings follow willing hearts.
Missionaries are not sent out to be taught by the world’s ideas but to teach what the Lord has given them, by the Spirit’s power.

f.w: Ye are not sent forth to be taught, but to teach

n: They themselves will be taught from heaven. If they sanctify themselves, they will be “endowed with power”—a promise later tied to the Kirtland Temple.
The “great day of the Lord”—his Second Coming—is near, so this is no time for distraction.

f.w: the great day of the Lord is nigh

n: A dramatic picture of the Lord’s coming: heaven and earth shake and a trumpet calls the righteous dead to rise, while the wicked dead must wait for a later resurrection.

f.w: ye sinners stay and sleep until I shall call again

n: Therefore, prepare for action and holiness, so you are not counted among the wicked when that day comes.

f.g: Literally, tuck up long robes for work or travel; figuratively, get ready.

n: Elders are to raise their voices boldly and warn everyone—young and old, enslaved and free—to prepare for the Lord’s coming.
If people reject the Lord when he calls through mortal messengers, how will they respond when nature itself thunders the same message? Warnings will grow louder if ignored.

f.w: if I, who am a man
f.g: The Lord here speaks of calling through his human servants, or of himself as one who once lived as a man.

n: Lightning flashing from east to west will join the call to repent. In scripture, signs in nature often function as God’s voice.

f.w: the lightnings shall streak forth from the east unto the west

n: Finally, the Lord himself will speak from heaven to all nations, reminding them that he is their Creator.
Using Jesus’s tender image from his lament over Jerusalem, the Lord mourns that he has often tried to gather the nations to safety, but they refused.

f.w: as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings

n: A sweeping list of the ways God calls his children: prophets, angels, his own voice, natural disasters, judgments, mercy, and the promise of eternal life. Every voice has the same purpose—to save—but many still refuse.

f.w: by the voice of judgment, and by the voice of mercy

n: The cup of God’s anger is full—the time of judgment has come for the persistently wicked. A “cup” is a biblical image for one’s allotted portion.

f.w: the cup of the wrath of mine indignation

n: The Lord seals his message: these are his own words.
This is the final call to work in the Lord’s vineyard—the world—before he comes. Compare the Book of Mormon’s allegory of the olive tree, where the servants labor one last time.

f.w: labor ye in my vineyard for the last time

n: In his own timing the Lord will come in judgment, and his redeemed people will reign with him on the earth.

f.w: shall reign with me on earth

n: The Millennium—a thousand years of peace foretold by prophets—will surely come.

f.g: Latin for “thousand years”; the period of Christ’s personal reign on earth.

n: Satan will be bound during the Millennium. Afterward he will be released briefly before the final end of the earth as we know it.
The righteous living at that time will be changed to immortality instantly, and the earth will be transformed as if by fire.

f.w: changed in the twinkling of an eye

n: The fate of the wicked is described as unquenchable fire, but its full nature is not revealed to mortals; it will be known at the judgment.
Jesus Christ names himself and asks the elders to treasure these words and let the seriousness of eternity weigh on their minds.

f.w: Treasure these things up in your hearts

f.g: The weighty, serious realities of eternal life and judgment.

n: A brief closing charge: be serious-minded and keep every commandment.
